signals.summary: A cluster of fresh sleep-science coverage is converging on the sleep ENVIRONMENT rather than the sleeper: cooler bedrooms, morning sunlight, dimming the room and de-emphasizing blue light. This serves perfectly as calm interior/object imagery (linen, blackout dark, a cool blue pre-dawn window, a single low lamp).
signals.why_now: 4+ independent items in the last ~48h: U of Utah Health on cooler bedroom temp (7.2h), bgr on debunking blue light (22.9h), PsyPost on morning sunlight and sleep timing (40.4h), Nature on diet and sleep quality (48.7h), plus a high-engagement HN essay 'Where Human Sleep Went Wrong' (53.5h, 129 pts). Evergreen Yoga With Adriene 'Legs Up The Wall / bedtime flow' support the ritual angle.

signals.summary: Mobility, flexibility and 'age-well' functional routines are surging across mainstream outlets — five-minute mobility flows, band work, moves for runners over 50, hand-strength for seniors. Best served through the RECOVERY CORNER as objects: a rolled mat, resistance bands coiled, a foam roller, yoga blocks in soft studio light (bodies score low here).
signals.why_now: 6 independent items within ~96h, several very fresh: Kern Valley Sun senior hand mobility (11.7h), Runner's World '5 moves for runners over 50' (19.2h), Tom's Guide 5 bodyweight mobility moves (78.2h), Telegraph PT 5-minute flexibility routine (80.2h), WBAL resistance-band mobility (93.2h), NYT/HN 'exercises PTs wish everyone did to age well' (94.5h).

signals.summary: Hyrox continues its global spread (Germany origin story, Chinese pensioners joining, explainer coverage). Producible without athletes by shooting the ARENA AND EQUIPMENT — sled, wall balls, SkiErg, rowing ergs, sandbags racked under stadium light.
signals.why_now: Sustained, still-live trend wave with 4-5 sources; freshest DW.com 'global fitness craze' (52.1h) and The Times 'Chinese pensioners jump to Hyrox' (74.4h), reinforced by ABC/Yahoo explainers and USA Today 'is Hyrox the new CrossFit'. Evergreen going-global framing keeps it current past the strict 48h line.

signals.summary: A 'gentler is better' wave: exercise snacks, ultra-slow running, short micro-efforts that 'don't feel like exercise'. Reads well as unpeopled place/object imagery — a quiet morning park path, a single kettlebell by the door, sunlit stairs, walking shoes on a mat.
signals.why_now: Fresh anchors: Us Weekly 'What Are Exercise Snacks?' (16.6h) and Canadian Running 'Korea's viral really-really-slow running' (64.4h), plus Newsweek/HN '3-minute exercise beats 90-minute workouts' (119.9h). Older ELLE/WSJ/NYPost 'do less / Zone 0' pieces show the theme has legs.

signals.summary: August is National Wellness Month, with coverage pivoting from surface self-care to calmer emotional-wellness rituals. Directly producible as still self-care environments: a steaming mug of tea, a candle, an open journal, a tidy bath corner, soft late-summer light.
signals.why_now: Two independent items in-window as the month runs out: WESH 'National Wellness Month: emotional health over surface-level self-care' (47.3h) and wimberleyview 'August is Wellness Month' (80.2h). Squarely seasonal for the 2026-08-21 late-summer moment.
